title: Beyond the Shadows of Plato's Cave: Evaluating False Memory in Autonomous Agents via Counterfactual Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2609.39473v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Autonomous agents increasingly rely on memory to generalize beyond their training environments. However, agents are bounded by what they have seen and believed, and leveraging such memories in unseen environments can introduce biases into their internal beliefs. We formalize this phenomenon as \textit{false memory}, which can arise from spurious correlations, environment shifts, and knowledge conflicts. Despite its importance, false memory is difficult to evaluate because it stems from agent internal beliefs and is easily confounded with ordinary generalization failures. Therefore, we propose FAME, a training-free framework that evaluates false memory through the evolution of agent beliefs under counterfactual reasoning. translated_title: 走出柏拉图洞穴的阴影：通过反事实推理评估自主智能体中的虚假记忆
translated_abstract: 自主智能体日益依赖记忆来超越其训练环境进行泛化。然而，智能体受限于其过往所见与所信的内容，在未见环境中利用此类记忆可能会给其内部信念引入偏差。我们将这一现象形式化为“虚假记忆”，它可能源于虚假相关、环境偏移和知识冲突。尽管十分重要，虚假记忆却难以评估，因为它源于智能体的内部信念，且极易与普通的泛化失败相混淆。因此，我们提出了FAME，一个免训练的框架，通过反事实推理下智能体信念的演化来评估虚假记忆。具体而言，反事实场景揭示了当记忆的潜在概念在假设干预下发生偏移时，信念如何随之变化；因此，测量由此产生的概念漂移提供了一个区分虚假记忆的信号。
tldr: 提出免训练框架FAME，利用反事实推理下智能体信念的概念漂移，来评估和识别自主智能体中难以检测的虚假记忆。
en_tdlr: Proposes FAME, a training-free framework that evaluates false memory in autonomous agents by measuring concept drift in agent beliefs under counterfactual reasoning.
